buttonLabel: "Explore routes through Guatemala, Honduras, Costa Rica and Panama"
lead: >-
  You can explore Guatemala, Honduras, Costa Rica and Panama on two extensive Ada Tours itineraries. One lasts 24 days and crosses six countries; the other takes 26 days and includes eight. Both feature Mayan cities, Costa Rica's tropical landscapes and Panama City, but the order of travel, transport and nature stops differ. Compare the complete itineraries rather than just the four countries they share.
---

## Four countries, two different ways to travel across Central America

**The countries in this selection overlap, but the itineraries are not identical.** [Best of Central America](/multi-country/tour/best-of-central-america/) is a 24-day journey through Guatemala, Honduras, El Salvador, Nicaragua, Costa Rica and Panama. [Central America: 8 Countries in 26 Days](/multi-country/tour/central-america-8-countries-26-days/) starts farther north in Mexico, then includes Belize before continuing through the region's other principal countries.

Our catalogue features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. **The four countries in this selection do not mean that either trip visits only those four:** both itineraries cover a wider area.

| Itinerary | Key difference |
|---|---|
| 24 days, 6 countries | Starts in Guatemala, primarily overland transport |
| 26 days, 8 countries | Starts in Mexico, more flights |

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_luchshee_v_tsentralnoj_amerike,tour_central_america_eight_countries_26_days}}

## Guatemala and Honduras: comparing the order of historic sites

On the 24-day itinerary, the introduction to the region begins in [Antigua Guatemala](/guatemala/place/antigua-guatemala/). Next come an ascent of Pacaya Volcano, villages around Lake Atitlán, the Chichicastenango market, [Tikal and Flores](/guatemala/place/tikal-and-flores/), Río Dulce and Quiriguá. In Honduras, travellers visit the [Copán ruins](/honduras/place/copan-ruinas/), known for their carved stelae and Hieroglyphic Stairway.

On the 26-day journey, Guatemala comes after Mexico and Belize. The itinerary also includes [Tikal](/guatemala/place/tikal-and-flores/), Antigua, Pacaya and Atitlán, but in a different order. Copán follows, then the route continues towards El Salvador.

If Mayan history is your main interest, compare the time spent at archaeological sites instead of simply counting countries. [Tikal](/guatemala/place/tikal-and-flores/) lies within tropical forest, while [Copán](/honduras/place/copan-ruinas/) is particularly distinguished by its sculpture and inscriptions. Both are UNESCO World Heritage sites, and each calls for its own sightseeing day.

## Costa Rica and Panama: different nature itineraries

The Costa Rican section of the 24-day journey covers [Arenal](/costa-rica/place/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/), Caño Negro, [Monteverde](/costa-rica/place/monteverde-santa-elena/), the [Tárcoles River](/costa-rica/place/tarcoles-river/) and [Manuel Antonio](/costa-rica/place/manuel-antonio/). The route then enters Panama, passing through Boquete and Barú Volcano before reaching [Panama City](/panama/place/panama-city/), Chagres and time to relax on the Pacific coast.

In the 26-day version, [Tortuguero](/costa-rica/place/tortuguero/) follows Monteverde and Arenal, with excursions along its canals. The Panama section is shorter: [Chagres](/panama/place/chagres-national-park/), an Emberá village, the capital and the [Panama Canal](/panama/place/panama-canal/).

The 24-day journey is therefore more suitable if you want Pacific-side parks and more time in Panama. The 26-day alternative gives dedicated attention to Caribbean Tortuguero and combines it with Mexico and Belize.

## Getting around: why the itineraries differ

The 24-day journey is largely overland, with some domestic flights and water crossings; the itinerary mentions a ferry on the way from El Salvador to Nicaragua. The 26-day alternative involves more separate flights, including San Salvador to Managua, Managua to San José, and onward to Panama. These are different transport arrangements; a flight or ferry mentioned in an itinerary does not replace checking schedules for your chosen travel date.

Time spent at borders and connections affects the hours available for sightseeing. Visa and transit planning must cover **every country on each complete itinerary**: six or eight, respectively. Requirements depend on nationality, travel documents, itinerary and length of stay.

## Seasons, altitude and costs

Antigua and Atitlán lie in the mountains and can be cooler than Copán. [Monteverde](/costa-rica/place/monteverde-santa-elena/) is humid and frequently misty, while Costa Rica's Pacific coast has different seasonal patterns from Caribbean Tortuguero. A relatively drier period in many Pacific regions generally falls between December and April, although conditions should be checked for each stop.

Bring sun and rain protection, footwear suitable for volcanic and forest trails, and medical travel insurance covering every country and planned activity. Compare flight, accommodation, entrance and transport costs on the same basis. If the tours use different currencies or include different services, the number of days alone is not an adequate comparison.

## Frequently asked questions

### Which countries are included in the 24-day itinerary?

Guatemala, Honduras, El Salvador, Nicaragua, Costa Rica and Panama.

### Which tour includes Mexico and Belize?

The 26-day itinerary through eight countries. Those two countries are added to the four selected countries and the intermediate stops.

### Which itinerary includes Tortuguero?

The 26-day itinerary. The 24-day journey instead includes Manuel Antonio and additional stops on the Pacific side.

### Can I book a tour that visits exactly these four countries?

That would require a separately designed itinerary: both existing journeys pass through additional countries.

buttonLabel: "Active adventures in Guatemala, Costa Rica, Honduras and Panama"
lead: >-
  The 26-day Central America itinerary includes a hike on Pacaya Volcano, a walk to El Tigre Waterfalls, a canopy experience in Monteverde and a river journey along the Chagres to an Emberá village. Honduras adds ancient Copán. Discover which activities require fitness, which are leisurely excursions and how transfers between these countries work.
---

## Four adventure destinations within an eight-country itinerary

For a combination of [Costa Rica](/costa-rica/), [Guatemala](/guatemala/), [Honduras](/honduras/) and [Panama](/panama/), we offer {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}: [Central America: 8 Countries in 26 Days](/multi-country/tour/central-america-8-countries-26-days/). The journey also visits Mexico, Belize, El Salvador and Nicaragua. **There is currently no separate four-country itinerary on offer here.**

The activities follow a clear sequence: a volcano hike in Guatemala, walking and forest excursions in Costa Rica, and a river trip in Panama. Honduras contributes a historic site visit where the physical activity consists mainly of walking.

| Country | Actual itinerary |
| --- | --- |
| Guatemala | Pacaya and Lake Atitlán |
| Honduras | Copán ruins |
| Costa Rica | Monteverde, El Tigre, Arenal |
| Panama | Chagres and the Emberá |

## Guatemala: from Tikal to Pacaya Volcano

After crossing the border from Belize on day eight, the group visits [Tikal](/guatemala/place/tikal-and-flores/), an ancient Maya complex surrounded by tropical forest. The following day includes [Antigua Guatemala](/guatemala/place/antigua-guatemala/) and an introduction to traditional weaving in local villages.

Day ten features a hike on [Pacaya](/guatemala/place/pacaya-volcano/), **from approximately 1,900 to 2,300 metres above sea level**. This is one of the trip's specific walking activities. After descending, the route continues towards [Lake Atitlán](/guatemala/place/lake-atitlan/).

Pacaya is an active volcano. Trail access, weather, altitude changes and physical fitness all need to be considered. The confirmed itinerary **does not include** reaching the summit at approximately 2,552 metres: promising to conquer the crater would be inaccurate.

The following day, travellers visit San Juan La Laguna and Santiago Atitlán and cross part of the lake by boat. This is a day of culture and scenery, rather than a strenuous mountain activity.

## Honduras: Copán and the opportunity to explore Maya heritage

On day 12, travellers arrive in [Copán Ruinas](/honduras/place/copan-ruinas/); the next day they explore the ancient complex, its stelae and the Hieroglyphic Stairway. They then travel on to El Salvador.

**This Honduras section does not include a separate rafting, rock-climbing or multi-day trekking programme.** Visiting Copán involves walking through an archaeological site and focuses primarily on history. UNESCO recognises Copán for its monumental architecture and carved stone monuments.

If you are seeking exclusively adventure-based travel with demanding activities every day, consider this a cultural interlude. It helps you understand Central America, but offers a different experience from climbing a volcano.

## Costa Rica: the most varied active section

Following a flight from Managua to San José, the group heads to [Monteverde](/costa-rica/place/monteverde-santa-elena/). Day 19 includes a cloud-forest walk and a canopy activity. You may spot a quetzal if you are lucky, although sightings cannot be guaranteed.

Day 20 includes an approximately three-hour hike to [El Tigre Waterfalls](/costa-rica/place/el-tigre-waterfalls/). The trail involves river crossings and rocky sections; the source itinerary rates the difficulty as moderate to challenging. A light snack and around 35 minutes of horseback riding are included at the end.

The group then travels to [La Fortuna and Arenal Volcano](/costa-rica/place/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/). On day 21, the itinerary includes hanging bridges and a walk across an area of former lava flows. Costa Rica's national protected areas system describes the Arenal area as protecting volcanic and forest ecosystems, with regulated trails for visitors.

**Fitness requirements deserve particular attention at El Tigre.** River crossings, wet rocks and climbs may be more demanding than a city tour. The confirmed programme does not establish that this stretch can be completed without physical exertion or guarantee an alternative format suitable for every traveller.

## Panama: Chagres, a waterfall and an Emberá village

On day 25, travellers leave [Panama City](/panama/place/panama-city/) for [Chagres National Park](/panama/place/chagres-national-park/). Between 08:00 and 16:00, the programme includes a boat trip along the [Chagres River](/panama/place/chagres-river/), swimming near a waterfall and a visit to [Tusipono](/panama/place/tusipono-embera-village/), an Emberá village. Lunch, crafts, music and dancing are part of the visit.

This is an adventure on the water, but **not white-water rafting**. The main attractions are the river, forest, waterfall and contemporary culture of the community. Panamanian authorities highlight Chagres's natural importance and the need to observe visitor restrictions.

River levels can affect access. Parts of the park were temporarily closed in 2026 because of rising water. Conditions therefore need checking before travel; an earlier announcement that the park had reopened is no guarantee of access on every date.

Day 26 is devoted to [Panama City](/panama/place/panama-city/), the Miraflores Locks and historic districts, followed by departure. No separate sporting activity is planned for the final day.

## Why the four countries cannot simply be combined into an existing shorter tour

The actual trip includes other countries between those selected: Guatemala is followed by Honduras, then El Salvador and Nicaragua, and only then Costa Rica. From Costa Rica, the group flies to Panama. The intermediate countries cannot be removed while keeping every overnight stay, flight and border crossing unchanged.

A journey covering only Guatemala, Honduras, Costa Rica and Panama would need new transport arrangements and a separate agreement on services, duration and price. The tour is not sold as an automatically assembled set of four independent modules.

## Preparation and suitable seasons

The itinerary combines Guatemala's volcanic highlands, Costa Rica's humid forests and Panama's river landscapes. Weather conditions vary between these areas. Heavy rainfall can change trail, waterfall and boat-trip conditions. Grippy outdoor shoes, a rain jacket, spare dry clothing and readiness for early departures are generally more useful than carrying extensive equipment.

Before choosing dates, check entry rules for each traveller's nationality, connections and baggage allowances on regional flights. Individual medical advice is appropriate for health considerations, particularly where exertion and altitude are involved. Ada Tours can coordinate itinerary details; changes to included services are agreed separately.

Other journeys with active days can be found in our [Adventure collection](/interests/adventure/). Compare the actual trails and the hours allocated to them, rather than just counting countries.

## Frequently asked questions about the adventure itinerary

### Does Pacaya include a full ascent to the summit?

No. The planned hike climbs from approximately 1,900 to 2,300 metres. The summit is not included in the itinerary.

### How long is the hike to El Tigre Waterfalls?

Approximately three hours, including river crossings and rocky sections. Difficulty is rated moderate to challenging.

### Will there be rafting on the Chagres?

The trip includes a boat excursion along the river, not white-water rafting.

### Is there a ready-made tour visiting only these four countries?

This page describes an eight-country journey. A four-country alternative would need to be planned and priced separately.

status: approved
buttonLabel: "Beach time in Costa Rica, Guatemala, Honduras and Panama"
lead: >-
  Among journeys connecting Costa Rica, Guatemala, Honduras and Panama, the beach portion of the longer itinerary falls at Manuel Antonio and on the final Pacific-coast days at Playa Blanca. Guatemala and Honduras are devoted to volcanoes, Lake Atitlán and Maya cities. When choosing a tour, look at the actual free days, hotel locations and transfers, rather than simply the four countries listed in the selection.
---

## Where beach time is actually scheduled

**Beach time is concentrated in Costa Rica and Panama.** The relevant [24-day Best of Central America itinerary](/multi-country/tour/best-of-central-america/) covers Guatemala, Honduras, El Salvador, Nicaragua, Costa Rica and Panama. All four selected countries are part of its main route, but the journey also visits two others. The [complete catalogue for this country combination](/multi-country/costa-rica_guatemala_honduras_panama/) includes tours with different themes: a coastline on the map does not automatically mean days free by the ocean.

Day 17 in Costa Rica includes [Manuel Antonio National Park](/costa-rica/place/manuel-antonio/). After a nature walk, there is an opportunity to spend time on the park's beaches. The journey then continues across the Panamanian border, through mountainous Boquete and Barú Volcano to Panama City. **The main beach stay comes at the end of the trip:** on days 22 and 23 at [Playa Blanca](/panama/place/playa-blanca/), there are no compulsory excursions, leaving time for the ocean and resort facilities.

This sequence suits travellers who want to discover Central America first and relax afterwards. Anyone looking for a week devoted exclusively to beaches may find a journey with so many overland borders and excursions too busy.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_luchshee_v_tsentralnoj_amerike}}

## Costa Rica: a nature walk with time by the sea

At [Manuel Antonio](/costa-rica/place/manuel-antonio/), the nature and beach experiences sit side by side. The day begins in the national park, where humid forest meets the Pacific coast. After the walk, you can enjoy time on the park's beaches. Access is regulated by SINAC; current visiting rules, tickets and open sections should be checked when choosing travel dates.

Previous Costa Rican stops have different purposes: the [Arenal area](/costa-rica/place/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/) is about volcanic scenery, [Monteverde](/costa-rica/place/monteverde-santa-elena/) about cloud forest, and Tárcoles about a river excursion. Their inclusion does not increase the number of beach days. Allow time on the coast after the walking activities, and pack closed shoes for trails as well as light clothing for the ocean.

## Guatemala and Honduras: cultural stops between nature experiences

The Guatemala section includes [Antigua](/guatemala/place/antigua-guatemala/), an ascent of [Pacaya Volcano](/guatemala/place/pacaya-volcano/), [Lake Atitlán](/guatemala/place/lake-atitlan/) and [Tikal](/guatemala/place/tikal-and-flores/). The route also follows Río Dulce through Livingston; its river and cultural stops are not equivalent to a scheduled Caribbean beach holiday.

In Honduras, the principal stop is [Copán](/honduras/place/copan-ruinas/) and its Maya monuments. The programme does not include beach days on the Honduran islands. When using this four-country selection, distinguish between **visiting a country** and **actually spending time on its beaches**. The itinerary appeals to travellers who want archaeology together with the ocean, while those hoping to swim every day need a different balance.

## Panama: why the beach stay follows Boquete and Chagres

Before the beach break, Panama's itinerary includes mountainous Boquete, a jeep trip to Barú Volcano and an introduction to the Panama Canal. An excursion to [Chagres National Park](/panama/place/chagres-national-park/) then combines a river journey, a visit to an Emberá village and swimming near a waterfall. Afterwards, travellers move to a Pacific-coast resort.

**Days 22 and 23 have no compulsory excursions.** Accommodation is at Playa Blanca Beach Resort, with breakfasts included. Day 24 is reserved for the airport transfer, so it should not be counted as a third full beach day. If you would like more days by the ocean, their duration and accommodation need to be agreed as an itinerary change.

Wind, rain, sea conditions and the resort's own rules matter for time by the water. The trip passes through mountain and coastal regions, making a single "Central America season" too broad to describe every stop. We help coordinate transfers and free days around the chosen programme.

## Flights, borders, money and luggage

Before reaching the beach section, travellers cross several borders and take domestic flights. The specified programme includes flights from Guatemala City to Flores and from David to Panama City. On a long itinerary, baggage allowances of the actual carriers, sufficient time between road transfers and flights, and allowances for border formalities all matter.

**Entry requirements must be checked for all six countries**, not merely the four named in the catalogue heading. Nationality, transit airports, passport validity and the sequence of border crossings may affect the necessary documents. National currencies and payment methods also differ: do not assume that one bank card or US-dollar cash will be accepted everywhere.

You will need varied clothing: lightweight sun-protective items for the coast, a rain jacket for the tropics, closed shoes for archaeological sites and a warm jacket for the early mountain departure to Barú. We discuss connections, transfers and baggage requirements as part of planning the specific trip, while official rules must still be checked.

## Frequently asked questions about beach holidays in these four countries

### Are beach days included in Guatemala and Honduras?

No. In the confirmed itinerary, these countries are devoted to volcanoes, cities and Maya monuments. Time by the sea is planned in Costa Rica and especially during the final part of the stay in Panama.

### How much free time is available on Panama's beaches?

Two days, days 22 and 23. An airport transfer is scheduled for the following day. Changing the number of free days requires an itinerary adjustment.

### Can I travel only through the four countries named in the title?

Our collection features trips that pass through all four, but the complete journey may include other destinations. [Best of Central America](/multi-country/tour/best-of-central-america/) also includes El Salvador and Nicaragua. Removing them requires a separately agreed itinerary.

### Is this tour suitable for a primarily beach-focused holiday?

It is better suited to a sightseeing journey with time by the ocean at the end. The route includes archaeology, volcanoes, early starts and transfers. For a primarily beach-based trip, compare [other beach holidays](/interests/beach-holidays/) by their number of free days.

lead: >-
  One extensive journey can take you from Maya cities in Guatemala and Honduras to Antigua's colonial streets, modern Panama and the traditions of an Emberá community. In the available itineraries, Costa Rica primarily adds days in nature. Explore how culture fits into the two longer journeys and which countries they visit beyond these four.

## From Tikal and Copán to the Panama Canal

Journeys combining culture and history across Costa Rica, Guatemala, Honduras and Panama reveal several very different chapters of Central American history. In [Guatemala](/guatemala/) and [Honduras](/honduras/), the principal theme is the Maya civilisation. [Panama](/panama/) combines colonial history with the Panama Canal and visits to present-day local communities. In the available itineraries, [Costa Rica](/costa-rica/) is predominantly devoted to nature: forests, volcanoes and protected areas. This matters to travellers choosing a journey primarily for museums and monuments.

Our catalogue includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. **Both available itineraries visit more than four countries.** This page highlights where those journeys overlap across the four countries under the Culture and History theme; it does not promise a separate four-country tour with direct transfers between each neighbouring country.

## Guatemala and Honduras: Maya history in different cities

At [Tikal and Flores](/guatemala/place/tikal-and-flores/), temples rise above the forests of Petén. UNESCO lists the archaeological site of Tikal as World Heritage under both cultural and natural criteria. Its ancient plazas and temple structures offer insight into the political and religious life of one of the Maya world's major centres.

[Antigua Guatemala](/guatemala/place/antigua-guatemala/) reflects a different era, with Spanish colonial architecture, churches, cobblestone streets and an urban layout against a backdrop of volcanoes. Around [Lake Atitlán](/guatemala/place/lake-atitlan/), travellers encounter local settlements and cultural traditions. The full 24-day itinerary also includes the archaeological site of Quiriguá and the Chichicastenango market; the 26-day itinerary visits the villages of San Juan La Laguna and Santiago Atitlán.

At [Copán](/honduras/place/copan-ruinas/), the focus shifts to Maya stone sculpture and hieroglyphic inscriptions. The Hieroglyphic Stairway is particularly famous and provides a way of comparing Copán with Tikal through written monuments as well as pyramids. Both tours allocate a specific excursion day to Copán. **Honduras is primarily an archaeological stop in this selection:** safari activities, beach holidays and additional Honduran cities should not be assumed to be included simply because the country appears in the four-country combination.

## Panama: the city, canal and Emberá community

The final stages are associated with [Panama City](/panama/place/panama-city/) and the [Chagres National Park](/panama/place/chagres-national-park/) area. Here the journey moves from Maya cities to the history of transcontinental routes, the workings of the interoceanic canal and living cultural traditions.

The 26-day programme includes [Casco Viejo](/panama/place/casco-viejo/) and the Miraflores Locks. Panama's historic district reveals urban buildings from the colonial period, while the locks help explain how the modern waterway crosses the isthmus. Both programmes include a trip to Chagres and an introduction to Emberá culture; the 26-day itinerary specifically names [Tusipono village](/panama/place/tusipono-embera-village/).

Visiting the community should be approached as a meeting with contemporary people, their crafts and customs. The exact format, permission to take photographs or video, and duration of the visit depend on the confirmed itinerary and the host community's rules. Water levels on the Chagres also influence the boat portion of the visit.

## Why Costa Rica is included in a culture-focused selection

Both tours have a cultural theme when considered as a whole, but the Costa Rican section is mainly about nature. On the 26-day itinerary, this means [Monteverde](/costa-rica/place/monteverde-santa-elena/), [Arenal](/costa-rica/place/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/) and [Tortuguero](/costa-rica/place/tortuguero/). On the 24-day trip, it is Arenal, [Caño Negro](/costa-rica/place/cano-negro-wildlife-refuge/), Monteverde and [Manuel Antonio](/costa-rica/place/manuel-antonio/).

This is where archaeological sightseeing gives way to walks through cloud forests and other natural landscapes. If your main interests are archaeology, museums and historic cities, consider the [cultural and historical tours in Guatemala](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/guatemala/) and [Honduras](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/honduras/). If wildlife is more important, the [nature selection covering the same four countries](/multi-country/costa-rica_guatemala_honduras_panama/interests/wildlife/) is more relevant.

## Comparing the two available itineraries

**[Central America: 8 Countries in 26 Days](/multi-country/tour/central-america-8-countries-26-days/)** begins in Mexico and travels through Belize, Guatemala, Honduras, El Salvador and Nicaragua before continuing into Costa Rica and finishing in Panama. Cultural highlights include Tikal, Antigua, villages around Atitlán and Copán, followed by Panama City, Casco Viejo and a visit to an Emberá community. The programme involves flights between certain sections; airfares and the final list of accommodation require separate agreement.

**[Best of Central America](/multi-country/tour/best-of-central-america/)** lasts 24 days and visits six countries: Guatemala, Honduras, El Salvador, Nicaragua, Costa Rica and Panama. In Guatemala it explores Antigua, Atitlán, Tikal and Quiriguá in greater detail before continuing to Copán. In Panama, the focus is on Boquete, Panama City, Chagres and a Pacific-coast finish.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_central_america_eight_countries_26_days,tour_source_luchshee_v_tsentralnoj_amerike}}

Listing both programmes together makes it possible to compare their actual duration, country sequence and themed days. **Neither itinerary is limited to Costa Rica, Guatemala, Honduras and Panama.** Consider the entire route, not merely the four countries they have in common.

## Borders, seasons and time at heritage sites

Both itineraries include an overland crossing between Guatemala and Honduras. The CA-4 arrangement has specific provisions for Guatemala, Honduras, El Salvador and Nicaragua, but entry conditions depend on nationality, passport type and current decisions by immigration authorities. Costa Rica and Panama need to be checked separately. Before travel, we help establish the actual order of crossings and required documents, including transit and re-entry where applicable.

For archaeological days, check the opening hours and appropriate walking time in advance: Tikal and Copán cover extensive areas and their main complexes are explored outdoors. Steps and paths can be slippery during rainy months; evenings around Antigua and Atitlán can be cooler than in the lowland tropical forest. Rain and water levels are significant in Panama, especially when the programme includes the Chagres boat section. As of October 2026, Chagres National Park had reopened after a temporary closure in August, although access to specific river sections and visiting conditions must be checked for the travel dates.

Pack with the whole itinerary in mind: light clothing for humid heat, an extra layer for cooler highland evenings, a waterproof jacket and comfortable closed shoes for stone steps, forest trails and uneven streets. Hand-luggage limits on domestic flights and the rules for large suitcases depend on the tickets selected.

## Frequently asked questions about cultural travel across four countries

### Can I visit only these four countries, without Mexico, Belize or Nicaragua?

Both existing tours shown here also visit other countries. A journey limited to the selected four would require an individually planned and agreed route, duration, border arrangements and range of services.

### Where are the most important Maya sites on these itineraries?

The main archaeological days are in Guatemala and Honduras: Tikal and Copán, plus Quiriguá on the 24-day trip. Costa Rica and Panama provide other experiences on these journeys.

### Should I choose 24 or 26 days?

The 26-day journey adds Mexico and Belize and includes Panama's Casco Viejo. The 24-day programme spends more time on several stops in Guatemala and adds nature-focused days in Costa Rica and Panama. Compare the whole sequence, not just the two-day difference.

### Should a visit to Chagres be booked in advance?

Availability of river routes and community visits depends on the weather, river conditions, park rules and arrangements with local participants. We confirm the specific date and visiting conditions while planning the trip.

  A nature-focused route through Costa Rica, Guatemala, Honduras and Panama brings together highland Lake Atitlán, Pacaya Volcano, forested Tikal, Costa Rican reserves and the tropical Chagres River. In Honduras, however, the itineraries stop for Copán's monuments rather than an independent nature trek. ## From Guatemala's volcanoes to Costa Rica's forests and Panama's rivers

Our selection features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} whose main routes include [Guatemala](/guatemala/), [Honduras](/honduras/), [Costa Rica](/costa-rica/) and [Panama](/panama/). All four countries form part of the main routes of the featured tours, but the journeys also cover other countries. The [26-day tour through eight countries](/multi-country/tour/central-america-8-countries-26-days/) additionally travels through Mexico, Belize, El Salvador and Nicaragua; the [24-day Best of Central America tour](/multi-country/tour/best-of-central-america/) also visits El Salvador and Nicaragua.

The changing natural environments are a particular attraction of this combination. Guatemala has volcanic highlands and a lake ringed by volcanoes; Costa Rica has cloud forests and lowland tropical forests; Panama has river valleys and, on one tour, mountainous Barú. **Honduras is represented primarily by Copán in these itineraries.** Passing through the country does not automatically add a day in one of its national parks.

## Guatemala: Pacaya, Atitlán and the forests of Petén

Both journeys include [Pacaya Volcano](/guatemala/place/pacaya-volcano/) and [Lake Atitlán](/guatemala/place/lake-atitlan/). The 26-day itinerary specifically describes a hike on Pacaya from approximately 1,900 to 2,300 metres above sea level. This distinguishes it from a brief viewpoint stop: you need closed shoes, water and the ability to walk over uneven volcanic terrain. Volcanic conditions determine which parts of the trail are open on any given day.

Atitlán offers something different: volcanic slopes, open water and settlements along the shore. The itinerary includes [San Juan La Laguna](/guatemala/place/san-juan-la-laguna/) and [Santiago Atitlán](/guatemala/place/santiago-atitlan/), with a boat crossing. It is a gentler contrast to the Pacaya ascent, although boat outings still depend on wind and lake conditions.

Both routes include [Tikal and Flores](/guatemala/place/tikal-and-flores/). Tikal lies within the extensive forests of Petén. UNESCO recognises it as a World Heritage site of both cultural and natural significance. During the archaeological visit, travellers therefore experience the surrounding forest, although the programme focuses on a Maya city rather than a separate wildlife safari. The 24-day journey adds [Río Dulce](/guatemala/place/rio-dulce/) and a water route towards Livingston. The 26-day version has no separate Río Dulce section in Guatemala.

## Honduras: Copán's natural setting, without an invented safari

[Copán Ruinas](/honduras/place/copan-ruinas/) features on both itineraries. Visitors go there for temples, carved stelae and the Hieroglyphic Stairway. Green hills and trees surround the site, but the listed excursions do not include a separate trek through Honduras's mountain ecosystems.

Remember that nature experiences are distributed across **the entire multi-country journey**. Not every country is an equally substantial nature stop. Travellers looking specifically for a nature-focused journey through Honduras should explore the [country's nature-tour collection](/interests/nature/tours/honduras/) rather than assume additional hikes are included just because the four-country filter mentions Honduras.

## Costa Rica: high-altitude forest and aquatic ecosystems

The shared stops are [Monteverde](/costa-rica/place/monteverde-santa-elena/) and [Arenal](/costa-rica/place/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/). Monteverde lies in a mountain area where humid air forms clouds at forest level; around Arenal, the itineraries include hanging-bridge walks and routes through volcanic scenery. The 26-day itinerary mentions an area of lava flows left by past eruptions. Conditions vary: cloud forests are frequently damp and cool, while more exposed areas near the volcano require protection from sunshine and possible downpours.

The most striking difference comes later. [Central America: 8 Countries in 26 Days](/multi-country/tour/central-america-8-countries-26-days/) visits [Tortuguero](/costa-rica/place/tortuguero/) on the Caribbean coast and includes a dawn boat ride along the canals. [Best of Central America](/multi-country/tour/best-of-central-america/) instead combines [Caño Negro](/costa-rica/place/cano-negro-wildlife-refuge/), the [Tárcoles River](/costa-rica/place/tarcoles-river/) and [Manuel Antonio](/costa-rica/place/manuel-antonio/).

Both tours are suitable for forest walks. Choose the first for Caribbean canals, or the second for a combination of wetlands and Pacific-side forests. See also our [nature itineraries in Costa Rica](/interests/nature/tours/costa-rica/).

## Panama: Chagres and different mountain experiences

[Chagres National Park](/panama/place/chagres-national-park/) and the [Chagres River](/panama/place/chagres-river/) feature in both journeys. The boat trip to an Emberá community follows the forest-lined river. It provides an encounter with both the landscape and local culture. Travellers can experience a lowland river environment, although this visit is not a substitute for a specialised rare-wildlife observation programme.

On the 24-day journey, the route follows Costa Rica with a visit to [Boquete](/panama/place/boquete/) and a 4×4 excursion to [Barú Volcano](/panama/place/baru-volcano/). Choose it if you want to add another dedicated mountain experience in Panama alongside Pacaya. The 26-day itinerary does not include that excursion: its Panama section focuses on Chagres, the capital and the canal.

## Choosing a combination of nature and physical activity

| Travel goal | Confirmed place or activity |
|---|---|
| Hiking on volcanic terrain | Pacaya |
| Lake surrounded by volcanoes | Atitlán |
| Tropical forest and archaeology | Tikal |
| Cloud forest | Monteverde |
| Caribbean waterways | Tortuguero, 26 days |
| Wetlands | Caño Negro, 24 days |
| Tropical river | Chagres |
| Jeep excursion into the mountains | Barú, 24 days |

There is no single "best season" for every stop along this journey. Weather at altitude on Pacaya, on the humid trails of Monteverde and along Tortuguero's lowland canals can differ even on the same trip. Pack layers, protect your documents and equipment against heavy rain, and allow flexibility for boat transport and mountain excursions. Trail rules, road conditions and access to volcanoes must be checked for your actual dates.

## Frequently asked questions about the nature itinerary

### Do both tours include an ascent of Pacaya?

Both itineraries visit the [Pacaya volcanic area](/guatemala/place/pacaya-volcano/). The 26-day programme specifically describes hiking from approximately 1,900 to 2,300 metres. Actual trail access depends on park authorities and volcanic activity.

### Can I experience nature at Tikal if the excursion is archaeological?

Yes. [Tikal](/guatemala/place/tikal-and-flores/) is surrounded by Petén's tropical forests. However, the confirmed excursion focuses on the ancient city; sightings of particular animals are not guaranteed.

### Is there a dedicated nature day in Honduras?

Neither of these two itineraries includes a separately confirmed nature day in Honduras. The main stop is historic [Copán](/honduras/place/copan-ruinas/).

### Which itinerary includes a trip to Barú Volcano?

The [24-day tour](/multi-country/tour/best-of-central-america/) includes a 4×4 excursion to [Barú](/panama/place/baru-volcano/). The 26-day journey has a different set of stops in Panama.

### Which itinerary is better for boat excursions?

For Caribbean canals, choose the 26-day itinerary with [Tortuguero](/costa-rica/place/tortuguero/). For Costa Rican wetlands and Guatemala's Río Dulce, choose the 24-day itinerary. Compare the actual boat excursions and their duration.
